notes: Spruce explicitly records M. speciosa among four Mollia species with five outer long stamen cohorts and five inner shorter cohorts with different pollen/anther colours. Darwin independently examined M. speciosa. The congener therefore fails the frozen negative-architecture gate before pollination eligibility or exact sister ranking matters.

The Flora Brasiliensis treatment directly states that the exterior stamens are nearly twice as long as the interior stamens. This source-resolved congener therefore retains the case-defining fertile-stamen differentiation.

Spruce explicitly includes M. tomentosa among the four collected Mollia species with five outer long cohorts and five inner shorter cohorts. It is retained as an auditable congeneric morphology failure.

M. trimera is a newly described congener with trimerous calyx, corolla and outer androecium, explicitly divergent from the usual Mollia floral plan. The publicly accessible source does not establish that its fertile stamens satisfy the frozen heteranthery-absence criterion. The same paper notes that Mollia monophyly has not been tested and infrageneric relationships remain unknown, so neither morphology eligibility nor closest-congener ranking can be closed.

Current taxonomy recognizes additional Mollia species beyond the source-resolved historical set. The 1978 generic treatment describes the usual Mollia androecium as two whorls of five phalanges with the outer whorl longer than the inner, but the 2025 divergent M. trimera description demonstrates that species-level exceptions to the traditional floral plan must be audited rather than assumed away. Public evidence does not provide an exhaustive species-level negative-architecture screen or a resolved Mollia species tree.
